    Four-arrow fork dichotomies #

    Since a finite ray category has no parallel irreducible arrows, four arrows at one endpoint either admit four noncentral neighboring vertices or admit a single loop together with three noncentral neighbors.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.outgoingFourArrow_fork_dichotomy {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] [Finite C] [IsFiniteRayCategory C] (x : RayVertex C) (hfour : 4 ≤ Nat.card (OutgoingQuiverArrow x)) :
    (∃ (a : Fin 4 ↪ OutgoingQuiverArrow x), ∀ (i : Fin 4), (a i).fst ≠ x) ∨ ∃ (l : OutgoingQuiverArrow x), l.fst = x ∧ ∃ (a : Fin 3 ↪ OutgoingQuiverArrow x), Disjoint {l} (Set.range ⇑a) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin 3), (a i).fst ≠ x

    Four outgoing arrows in a finite ray category have exactly the following shape relevant to the affine-star obstruction: either four can be chosen with noncentral targets, or there is a loop and three further arrows with noncentral targets. Parallel-arrow cases do not occur.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.incomingFourArrow_fork_dichotomy {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] [Finite C] [IsFiniteRayCategory C] (z : RayVertex C) (hfour : 4 ≤ Nat.card (IncomingQuiverArrow z)) :
    (∃ (a : Fin 4 ↪ IncomingQuiverArrow z), ∀ (i : Fin 4), (a i).fst ≠ z) ∨ ∃ (l : IncomingQuiverArrow z), l.fst = z ∧ ∃ (a : Fin 3 ↪ IncomingQuiverArrow z), Disjoint {l} (Set.range ⇑a) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin 3), (a i).fst ≠ z
